sentences.text: Zhuchengceratops is an extinct ceratopsian dinosaur belonging to the family Leptoceratopsidae that lived in modern-day China during the Upper Cretaceous.
This animal possessed a particularly massive and deep mandible that was 50 centimeters long and thin transversely.
The genus Zhuchengceratops was first described in 2010 by Xu et al. with the type species Zhuchengceratops inexpectus.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is an incomplete articulated skeleton including the combined skull, maxilla, squamosal, jugal, quadrate, wings, outer ring, mandible, the first fourteen vertebrae, ribs, and some additional elements.
These fossils were discovered in 2008 alongside numerous articulated combined bones of the hadrosaurid Shantungosaurus.

Phylogenetic analysis by the authors suggests Zhuchengceratops is an advanced leptoceratopsid more closely related to Leptoceratops and Udanoceratops, although the internal relationships of this triplet remain unresolved.

Zhuchengceratops lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia. The time range for Zhuchengceratops is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
